feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Trump rejects Iran's latest ceasefire proposal
entry.summary: President Trump has rejected the latest Iranian proposal to end the conflict. Meanwhile, France is sending military support to Saudi Arabia in its war against Iranian-backed militants.

entry.title: Trump rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal. What it means for U.S. allies in the Gulf
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with former assistant secretary of defense for the Middle East Dana Stroul about the latest ceasefire proposal from Iran.

entry.title: Police in South Africa are investigating a spate of mass shootings
entry.summary: Nearly 30 people were killed in two separate mass shootings over the weekend in South Africa.

entry.title: 5 tips for parents worried about their kids' screen time and online safety
entry.summary: Parental monitoring can help protect kids from the harms of social media and excess screen time. Screen time boundaries plus early and open conversations about online habits can make kids less vulnerable.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: President Trump has rejected Iran's latest proposal to end the war, five men were arrested near a U.K. air base for an alleged terror plot, Trump's fight with the press leaves his events uncovered.

entry.title: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear discusses his new book, 'Go and Do Likewise'
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear about his new book "Go and Do Likewise."

entry.title: Nor'easter wallops Northeast coastal communities
entry.summary: Northeast coastal communities are assessing damage from an early-season nor'easter that brought high winds and lashing rain, coinciding with high tides from Virginia to southern Maine.

entry.title: Unarmed 911 teams are reshaping public safety in nearly 100 cities
entry.summary: Some communities dispatch mental health clinicians as an alternative to a police response for emergency calls. Researchers consider a program in Durham, North Carolina, to be a success.

entry.title: California health officials warn of possible measles exposure in 6 counties
entry.summary: California health officials are on the lookout for new measles cases, after someone with the vaccine-preventable disease rode a passenger train and busses through six counties.

entry.title: Smoke ecology studies what can be done to prevent harms from wildfire smoke
entry.summary: A new field of study called "smoke ecology" strives to understand the smoke blowing off wildfires, and whether anything can be done to protect the environment's inhabitants from it.
